title: A delivery opened before a rename is received under the new number
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test with 3 on hand.
  • Create an open purchase order for this test, purchase order 1, from any vendor, with a line for part A picked from the lookup, 2 ordered and none received.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Use a desktop browser that can open a second tab on the same ShopView address, signed in as the same user.
  • Start in browser tab 1 on purchase order 1 (Parts, then Purchase Orders, then open purchase order 1).
custom_steps:
1. In tab 1, click Receive.
  2. Open a second browser tab on the same ShopView address.
  3. In tab 2, click Parts in the top bar.
  4. In tab 2, click Inventory in the left menu.
  5. In tab 2, type part A's part number in the Search box.
  6. In tab 2, click the part A row.
  7. In tab 2, replace the Part Number with the new number.
  8. In tab 2, click Save.
  9. Switch back to tab 1 without reloading it.
  10. In tab 1, type an invoice number in the invoice number field.
  11. In tab 1, type 10.00 as the cost.
  12. In tab 1, type 2 as the received quantity.
  13. In tab 1, click Receive on the Receive screen.
  14. In tab 2, type the new number in the Search box.
  15. In tab 2, click Part Library in the left menu.
  16. In tab 2, type part A's old part number in the Search box.
  17. In tab 2, click Vendor Invoices in the left menu.
  18. In tab 2, open the vendor invoice you just received.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Receive screen opens in tab 1 for purchase order 1, with the line under part A's old number.

Step 2:

  • A second tab opens.

Step 3:

  • Tab 2 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 4:

  • Tab 2 shows the Inventory page.

Step 5:

  • Part A is listed in tab 2.

Step 6:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 7:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 8:

  • The rename is saved in tab 2.

Step 9:

  • Tab 1 still shows the Receive screen opened before the rename.

Step 10:

  • The invoice number shows what you typed.

Step 11:

  • The cost shows 10.00.

Step 12:

  • The received quantity shows 2.

Step 13:

  • The delivery is accepted.

Step 14:

  • Part A is listed under the new number with 5 Available (3 + 2 = 5).

Step 15:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 16:

  • No entry is listed for the old number: the receipt made no Part Library entry for it.

Step 17:

  • The Vendor Invoices list opens.

Step 18:

  • The vendor invoice's line reads the new number, although the Receive screen was opened before the rename.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S13-R19c: “For a line linked to the renamed part, accepting a delivery uses the part's current number, even when the Receive screen was opened before the rename. No Part Library entry is created for the old number. A hand-typed line (S13-R19a) is received under its own number.”

From: Tech plan "Parts Lifecycle Update — Technical Implementation Plan" (7 Oct 2026, written against PRD v22; re-shared by the QA lead on 27 Oct 2026, unchanged), read 27 Oct 2026

  • §3 Technical Decisions, D30: “S13-R19c: ReceiveADelivery.php:88,108 take the number posted by the Receive screen; for a line linked to an order item with a part_id, the handler resolves the number from that part's current entry instead, so a rename between opening and accepting is honored and no entry is created for the old number.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
